name: Rotten Ethel, Bog Hag

alignment.name: Evil
alignment.description:
Evil creatures don’t necessarily go out of their way to hurt people, but they’re perfectly willing to take advantage of the weakness of others to acquire what they want.
	Evil creatures use rules and order to maximize personal gain. They don’t care whether laws hurt other people. They support institutional structures that give them power, even if that power comes at the expense of others’ freedom. Slavery and rigid caste structures are not only acceptable but desirable to evil creatures, as long as they are in a position to benefit from them.

description: This is the size of a typical human and serves as a standard in the game. This category has no special rules.

traits.name: Unwholesome Presence
traits.details: If an enemy in the aura spends a healing surge to regain hit points, that enemy regains only half the normal hit points.

traits.name: Aquatic
traits.details: Ethel can breathe underwater. In aquatic combat, she gains a +2 bonus to attack rolls against non-aquatic creatures.

traits.name: Horrid Scuttle
traits.details: On an initiative count of 10 + her initiative check, Ethel shifts up to half her speed and uses claw frenzy as a free action. If she cannot use a free action to make this attack due to a dominating or stunning effect, then that effect ends instead of Ethel making her attack.

auras.name: Unwholesome Presence
auras.details: If an enemy in the aura spends a healing surge to regain hit points, that enemy regains only half the normal hit points.

effect.description: Ethel can shift up to 2 squares.

hit.description: psychic damage, and the target is dazed (save ends).

effect.description: Ethel alters her physical form to appear as a young female elf, half-elf, eladrin, or human until she uses change self again or until she drops to 0 hit points. To assume a specific individual’s form, Ethel must have seen that individual. Other creatures can make a DC 31 Insight check to discern that the form is a disguise.
